title: Explorers of the Woodlands - a critter-crawl unboxing
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xya7ZlFJ-x8

Daniel (@dungeondive) unboxes Explorers of the Woodlands, a forest-themed cooperative dice crawler for one to four players from designer Jeffrey Wood, just delivered to US backers. He backed it for the art and theming, and at roughly the size of Bag of Dungeon and Seven Moons it sits right at the edge of his small-box collection.

The rulebook covers exploration and adventure phases, four heroes (Zilia, Klor, Shavei and Bethos), a five-chapter campaign, an enraged-bosses advanced mode, and a random dungeon mode he expects to play most. A final page is marked not to be read until you finish the campaign. The tiles include crossroads and dead ends, so exploration should matter, and he likes a crawl set outdoors, much like Bag of Dungeon 2. The cardboard is heavy-duty, and the autumnal palette suits October to December.

The printed meeples for each hero are the highlight. He'd rather see the illustrator's actual art on a meeple or standee than a miniature that doesn't match it. The decks hold minions such as a fungus samurai, treasures from boots to a spell book, and events that look mostly combat, so he hopes there's more to do than attack. A Kickstarter-only card appears to add an alternate mode. The full review follows in the next episode.

----

Daniel prefers printed meeples to miniatures because they carry the game's real art. Where do you stand: sculpted minis or flat art?
